strengths: Strong empirical results with ~10× speedup over LDM-based methods and consistent improvements across multiple restoration tasks (RESIZE, Snow100k, Rain13K, LOL-v1, GoP)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including multiple metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, MUSIQ, CLIPIQA), extensive ablations, user studies, and generalization testing on unseen/mixed degradations
Insightful scale-space analysis showing coarse VAR scales capture degradations while fine scales preserve scene-level details, providing useful understanding of VAR's suitability for restoration
Well-engineered technical solution combining cross-attention conditioning, latent refinement transformer, and architectural choices (RoPE embeddings, PatchGAN discriminator) in a coherent framework
Demonstrates strong generalization performance on unseen and mixed degradation datasets compared to baseline methods
Detailed supplementary materials with 15 appendix sections covering architectural details, theoretical analysis, additional ablations, and qualitative results supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: primarily engineers existing components (VAR, cross-attention, latent refinement) for a new task rather than proposing fundamentally new methods; each component is a straightforward adaptation of existing techniques

Unfair baseline comparisons: FixWizard evaluated without structure correction module; AutoDIR's evaluation setup doesn't reflect intended use; limited VAR baselines despite claims of advantage; some recent strong methods missing

Overclaimed contributions: cross-attention for image conditioning is standard practice in image-to-image translation; LRT claimed as critical but shows only marginal quantitative improvements (~0.06dB PSNR gains) despite added complexity; novelty of being first VAR-based AiOR is somewhat vacuous

Efficiency claims need clarification: 10× speedup inherently comes from VAR's architecture (autoregressive vs. iterative diffusion) rather than RestoreVAR-specific contributions; missing detailed runtime breakdown and comparison with accelerated LDM variants

User study has limited statistical power: only 36 responses across 50 image selections with error margins suggesting weak significance; no participant expertise/demographics provided
Scale-space analysis is descriptive rather than prescriptive: shows VAR exhibits the property but does not prove RestoreVAR design optimally exploits it or guide specific architectural choices
